$comment: EXP-1992 (2026-11-19; the spec of `hostCases`): ONE CALL HOST FOR THE DESKTOP APP AND THE CLI DAEMON. What a host does around `callStep` while it runs a call is one pure machine (`etalk::call::host`; replayed by the Rust hosts only, like `hostVoice`: phones and web never host a call), and both hosts are shells around it: each hands in what happened, on its own clock in ms (`at`), and does what comes back, in order. INPUTS (`t`): `begin` (the ring's clock starts and the worker's `Call` goes out: a streamed call once the caller is on the line, never before, a call run here at its start; once), `tick` (every timer that is due fires, in this order: the ring's earliest answer at `callRingMs(random)` after `begin`, the `maxRingMs` give-up, the mic check at the later of the ring's answer and 1.5 s after the worker listened, `hostVoice.waitMs` after `begin`, `callSession.openingWaitMs` after the voice was in), the worker's `listening` (`CallListening`), `level`, `partial`, `speechStarted`, `said` and `listenFailed`, the agent's clip as the host has it (`voice {clip, preparing}`, `prepared` = the worker's `Voices`), the call session (`sessionAsked`, `session`), the agent's `reply` (the newest new row of the call's conversation that `shouldSpeak` takes, with its spoken text), what was said ending (`spoken`: done, or stopped) or never said (`notSpoken`), `mute`, the other side's `hungUp {reason?}`, the person's `end`, the host's own `fail {code}` (its worker died, the stream dropped) and `unstorable` (#EXP-1982). EFFECTS (`do`): `event` (a streamed call's `call_event`: every step `wire.control` forwards, and a failure's code BEFORE the hang-up), `flush` (barge-in), `listen` (the worker's `Call`; a call run here rings on its own output for at most `maxRingMs`), `mute`, `speak`, `stop`, `hangup` (the worker's), `end` (the caller is hung up on), `send` (an utterance: into the call's own session, null = the chat), `callEnded` and `toast` (`copy.failed`). THE RULES the rows lock, beside the sections below: a reply while the call still rings is never the call's, only a call session's opening line, said at the pickup; a reply's caption, the opening line's too, is its first sentence; an opening line that cannot be said fails the call `unavailable` (EXP-1930), any other reply that cannot be said listens on; a `listenFailed` fails as `no_microphone`, `not_granted`, `meeting`, `unavailable` or (anything else) `dropped`, and `downloading` rings on. What still differs between the hosts lies outside the call: the rings each answers, its worker's lifecycle (a desktop's stays loaded, a server's loads for a call and exits `serverIdleMs` after it), the reply watch's reads and the sends. EXP-1991 (2026-11-19; SUPERSEDES NEW-99's availability order and inputs and EXP-1857's `callTarget` input below where they differ): AVAILABILITY IS ONE DESKTOP'S OWN REASON. `callAvailability(input)` (`availabilityCases`) is only what `callTarget` reads for the first candidate when no desktop speaks: input = that desktop's `device` (its name), `online`, `speech` and `meeting`; first match wins: offline → `offline`; meeting → `meeting`; no `speech` row → `preparing`; speech `failed` → `voiceFailed`; `noGpu` → `noGpu`; else enabled (a downloading voice rings until it is ready). Since EXP-1857 `callTarget` passed the same `agent`, `here` and `busy` for every desktop, so the inputs `agent`, `platform`, `here` and `busy` and the reasons `noAgent`, `noVoiceDevice` and `notHere` never showed on any platform: they are gone, and so is `callTarget`'s `platform` input, which only fed them. A target found while `busy` is still `reasons.busy` (`callTarget`'s own). EXP-1982 (2026-11-19, decided by Danny): A HOST THAT CAN STORE NO WORD OF A CALL REFUSES IT AT THE RING. A clear call (the server did not seal it) into a chat the host can write nothing into without a key holder (none runs and none is coming) is joined only to fail it `unavailable`: on the daemon a KEYED chat (`sessions.sendTarget` names an epoch; it sends plaintext into a keyless one), on the desktop app any chat that is not a clear tree, no chat yet included (it seals every other send; a Local account aside). The refusal's toast is `copy.failed.unavailable`, like the busy and meeting refusals: nothing warms up or listens, no call session starts, and a caller that never joins is hung up after `ringTimeoutMs`. A sealed call keeps its own path (`seal.endReasons.noKey`). BACKSTOP: an utterance the server refuses for good (a 4xx other than 401, 408, 429) while the host could not seal it ends the call `dropped` instead of listening on; any other failed send keeps the call. Rust hosts only (the daemon and the desktop app); every caller already steps `failed`. FEED-272 (2026-11-18, phase 5 of #EXP-1943; the spec of `tabs`): CHAT / VOICE TABS ON THE CALL SURFACE, so the chat can be read and written while talking. At the top of every call surface (the phones' full screen, the web overlay over the agent chat, the desktop's in-window `CallPanel`) sits the filled SegmentedControl (the genUI `Tabs`, `fill`: the segments share the width, the same look x4; testId `tabs.testIds.tabs`, one segment per `tabs.order` entry: `tabs.copy.chat` testId `tabs.testIds.chat`, `tabs.copy.voice` testId `tabs.testIds.voice`). A call opens on `tabs.initial` (voice); the choice lives as long as the call (a new call opens on voice again). VOICE = the call surface exactly as before (everything below the tabs: avatar, name, timer/status, via, caption, the round buttons). CHAT = the agent's MAIN chat (the chat the call belongs to, never the call's own session of #EXP-1961), scrollable, with its normal composer; the call stays on top of it, under the tabs, as THE pill's row DOCKED (the `call-pill` / `call-controls` entry, no new component: the avatar small, the name over the timer (ringing: the status), VoiceWave sm, the round mute and the red end at the compact size; docked = the width of the chat column instead of `pill.width`, no drag handle, never draggable, height `pill.height`, testId `pill`). Typing on the Chat tab sends a NORMAL message to that main chat (the call reads it before its next answer, #EXP-1961). Switching tabs NEVER ends, mutes or re-dials the call; the phones' minimize (EXP-1681: the button at the surface's top leading corner, now left of the tabs on both tabs, and back / swipe down) and the desktop's floating pill are unchanged. Web: the call lives with the agent page, so moving inside it (the Chat tab, an opened item) keeps it; only leaving the agent page or closing the tab hangs up (as before). FEED-276 (2026-11-18, phase 1 of #EXP-1943 / #FEED-275): NOTHING IS SPOKEN BEFORE THE AGENT'S OWN VOICE IS IN. A call's `ready` (the worker's `CallListening`, which the ring already waits for: `answerCases`) now also waits for the agent's own voice on the HOST: its uploaded clip on disk AND the worker's Prepare with it done, so the opening line (and every reply after it) is said in the agent's voice, never the built-in stock voice while the clip still downloads. Pure `callVoiceReady(clip, waitedMs)` (`hostVoice.cases`, replayed by the Rust hosts only: phones and web never speak) with `clip` = `none` (the agent has no clip: the built-in voice IS its voice) · `installed` (on disk, prepared) · `installing` (landed during the ring, its Prepare not confirmed yet) · `fetching` (still downloading) · `failed` (the fetch failed) and `waitedMs` since the ring started; the answer is `ready`, `wait`, or `builtIn` (ready with the built-in voice, LOGGED on the host). none / installed = ready; failed = builtIn at once; fetching waits until `hostVoice.waitMs`, then builtIn; installing waits until `hostVoice.waitMs`, then ready (the opening queues behind that Prepare, so it is still the agent's voice). `waitMs` 8000 stays inside the ring's usual 3 to 9 s and under the relay's `ringTimeoutMs` (a CLI daemon fetches the clip before it joins the call, bounded by `waitMs`). EXP-1941 (2026-11-18; CALL SEAL, the spec of `seal`; NOT ON YET: at this commit NO end seals, so the relay can still READ a call's events and audio. This is the contract and its vectors; the server op, the hosts (desktop app, CLI daemon: PR 8 and 9 of #EXP-1941) and the four callers follow, then the server turns it on): A CALL BETWEEN TWO SEALING ENDS IS SEALED END TO END; THE RELAY READS NOTHING BUT WHAT ROUTES OR ENDS IT. KEY (the message order of Noise NNpsk2, the tree secret as the psk): each end makes a fresh X25519 key per socket. The CALLER's HELLO, `seal.helloBytes.caller` bytes = version `seal.version` ‖ role (`seal.roles`) ‖ epoch u32 BE ‖ rootId (16 raw UUID bytes; a caller without a root sends zeros) ‖ eph[32], made once and resent unchanged. The HOST's, `seal.helloBytes.host` bytes = the same 54 with its role, then tag[16]; it exists only when the host has the key and is sent once. dh = X25519(own eph secret, peer eph), an all-zero result is refused; transcript = `seal.domain` ‖ callId[16] ‖ agentId[16] ‖ SHA-256(utf8(deviceId)) ‖ callerHello ‖ the first 54 bytes of the host's hello (188 bytes; never the tag); key(label) = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = dh ‖ clamp(S), salt = transcript, info = label, 32 bytes) for the four `seal.labels`, where S is the 32 SECRET bytes of the tree key of the HOST hello's root and epoch (never the public half) and clamp is X25519's (S[0] &= 0xF8; S[31] = (S[31] & 0x7F) | 0x40). The host's tag = ChaCha20-Poly1305(key(`seal.labels.downHello`), nonce twelve zero bytes, AAD = the 54 hello bytes before it, empty plaintext): the host's PROOF that it holds S and saw the same two hellos. The host's finish gives its hello with the tag; the caller's finish takes it with the root and the epoch the caller's OWN `sessions.sendTarget` answer names, refuses a hello that names others, and opens the tag, so a caller that has a sealer has the host's proof. The caller's proof is its first frame that opens: before it a host's sealer seals nothing. The handshake FINISHES ONCE: it wipes its eph secret, and a second finish is refused, also after one that failed. CIPHER: ChaCha20-Poly1305, tag 16 bytes, nonce = eight zero bytes ‖ ctr u32 BE; one key and one counter per direction and channel, from 0, plus 1 per frame sealed, never set from outside; the frame with ctr 4294967295 is the last, the next seal is refused. AUDIO (binary, the kinds of `wire.kinds`): byte 0 kind ‖ byte 1 type (`seal.frameTypes`) ‖ ctr u32 BE, these six bytes clear and the AAD, then the sealed plaintext seq u16 BE ‖ flags u8 ‖ len u16 BE ‖ packet[len] ‖ zeros up to exactly ONE `seal.audioPadStep` of the direction (never a second size: a packet above the step is refused by the sealer and the sender seals a frame with len 0 in its place), then the tag: 27 bytes plus the step. Flags bit 0 on `up` = the microphone is muted (a sealed call sends no `call_mute`); senders set the other bits to 0. The receiver opens only a ctr above the last it accepted and learns how many frames are missing before it; it trusts len alone, ignores the bytes behind the packet and flag bits it does not know, never refuses by seq, and hands a frame with len 0 to no decoder: such a frame stands for ONE packet its sender could not seal, carries that packet's seq, and counts as one missing frame more. A hello going up is the binary frame kind `up` ‖ type hello ‖ the hello. CONTROL (host → caller only, inside today's `call_event`): `{t: 'hello', data}` = base64url of the host's hello (94 chars), and `{t: 'sealed', data}` = base64url(ctr u32 BE ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag) with the ctr as AAD; the plaintext is ONE control frame of today as JSON text, padded with spaces to a multiple of `seal.controlPadBytes` and at most `seal.maxPlainBytes`; the ctr is strict (the first is 0, then exactly last + 1). STAYS READABLE: the ticket claims and `call_ring`, `call_ready`, `call_alive`, `call_end {reason}`, a `call_event` `failed {code}`, the hello, bytes 0 to 5 of a binary frame, every length and time. `seal.inputs` gives `seal.derived`; a vector is replayed on a FRESH pair of ends made from them (a `keys` vector with its `with` in place), its `after` up frames opened by the HOST's object first (a `down` vector needs the caller's proof), a sealer brought to `ctr` by that many seals; every `seal.refused` entry is refused with its `reason` (a finish entry runs `first`, when it has one, before `peerHello`). A vector names the step it used, so a later `audioPadStep` leaves the vectors as they are. THE STEPS (`seal.modeCases`, pure `callSealStep(role, state, event)` ×4; `cap` is the device cap a host that can seal advertises): each end learns the mode from the SERVER (`start`), never from a frame. A case feeds `events` from the idle state and expects the final `phase` and, per event, the `actions` in order: `timer` (start the `handshakeMs` timer: the caller at its FIRST `call_ready`, the host when its socket opens; nothing restarts it), `hello` (the caller sends its hello and again every `helloEveryMs`; the host sends its hello ONCE), `helloStop`, `key` (the key source: root and epoch from the server, the secret from the keyring or a pull every `pullEveryMs`), `finish` (once), `go` (the caller starts its microphone; the host steps `Ready`), `count` (drop the frame, count it), `end` / `end:<reason>` (`call_end`, reasons `seal.endReasons`), `fail:<code>` (the caller's toast), `abandon` (the key source stops, a late answer is dropped). The FIRST well-formed hello (its length, version and role) is taken on arrival, once; another hello or `call_ready` changes nothing. Before an end is sealed ONE thing of its own ends the call: the timer, `no_key`. A caller that gets clear content, a `sealed` event or a binary frame before it is sealed, or whose finish fails, ends `seal`; a host drops and counts what does not open. Once sealed, clear content or a `sealed` event that does not open ends `seal` at once, and `maxOpenFailures` audio frames in a row that do not open end `seal`. Every seal failure reads `copy.failed.dropped`. A clear `failed {code}` ends the call with its toast in every state, but a code of `seal.ownDeviceCodes` (the caller's OWN device) is never taken from the wire and reads `dropped`. The host ends a call it answered at `constants.maxCallMs` itself, sealed or clear. `required` (false): when true, an end that is not told `seal` makes no call. `maxLostMs` is the STARTING value of the host's rule for lost audio (it never joins across a gap; an utterance in which more than this is missing in total is not sent, and the caption returns to listening as after a sound that was no speech); it is set from a measurement on real calls before sealing is turned on. EXP-1942 (2026-11-18; Android BACKGROUND, SUPERSEDES the moment of the service start in EXP-1940 below): ANDROID HOLDS ITS MICROPHONE SERVICE FROM THE TAP. The `microphone` foreground service with its ongoing `Call {agent}` notification starts when the person taps call (the app is in front then, the one moment Android allows it; a missing RECORD_AUDIO grant is asked first, as before), BEFORE the ticket and the dial, never at `call_ready`; the ring is unchanged. Leaving the app DURING THE RING therefore keeps the call: when the host answers the microphone is live without the app coming back. One call holds one service: a second start while it is held starts nothing. Cancel during the ring, a refused `startCall`, a failed call and every other end stop it. The EXP-1940 rule stays as the fallback: a start Android still refuses (at the tap, or its `startForeground` afterwards) fails the call `dropped` (`copy.failed.dropped`) before it dials and never crashes the app. iOS is unchanged (iOS BACKGROUND below). EXP-1940 (2026-11-17): THE PHONE'S OUTPUT FOLLOWS THE ROUTE. A headset (wired, USB or Bluetooth) wins over the speaker button's loudspeaker or earpiece whenever one is on, also one that connects or leaves MID-CALL: the phone picks the output again on every route change (iOS re-applies its override on `routeChangeNotification`, Android on every audio device added or removed) and the `speaker` state stays what the person chose. A DIAL NEVER OUTLIVES ITS CALL: Cancel (or any end) while the caller's socket still connects closes the socket that connects afterwards, so the relay never rings a desktop for a call nobody is on. ANDROID'S MICROPHONE SERVICE STARTS OR THE CALL FAILS: at `call_ready` Android starts its `microphone` foreground service; when Android refuses it (the app is not in front at that moment, or it left before the service went foreground) the phone could not capture, so the call fails `dropped` (`copy.failed.dropped`) instead of running silent, and a refused service never crashes the app (#ERR-11). EXP-1929 (2026-11-17): REPLY AUDIO LEAVES AT REAL TIME. The host's speech worker sends a streamed call's reply at most 200 ms ahead of the clock (on average one `down` frame per `constants.frameMs`, inside the relay's `maxFramesPerSecond`, so no frame of a long reply is dropped) and steps `replyFinished` once the reply has played, never when its synthesis ended. A rung desktop starts the call only on the relay's `call_ready`: a ring cancelled before the admit (the relay answers `no_such_call`) starts nothing there and ends silently. EXP-1929: A DEAD CALL PATH IS NOTICED. Once paired, the relay sends `{t:'call_alive'}` (and a WebSocket ping) to both sockets every `constants.aliveMs`, and ends the call `idle` when EITHER socket sent nothing at all (an audio frame, a control frame or a pong) for `constants.idleTimeoutMs`, beside the rule that no audio either way for that long ends it: a silent host that answers the ping lives, a host that vanished is seen even while the caller streams. Each end (the host, every caller) that got a `call_alive` ends the call as dropped after `constants.idleTimeoutMs` without any frame from the relay (`callPathDead`, `livenessCases`: the host as a drop, the caller `failed dropped`); before its first `call_alive` (an older relay) it keeps no deadline. Additive: older builds ignore `call_alive` and answer the ping by themselves. EXP-1858 (voice per agent, phase c of #EXP-1847, 2026-11-15; EXTENDS EXP-1857 below): A CALL RINGS THE AGENT'S SERVER. `callTarget` input gains `servers` = the member's OWN servers (`devices.kind` `server`: a CLI daemon), the same `{id, name, online, speech, meeting}` rows (meeting always false), absent = none. The agent's device is a candidate when it is one of the member's own desktops OR servers; a server is NEVER `here` and NEVER a fallback (it speaks only for the agents that run on it), so the order stays: the agent's device, the desktop you're at, the other desktops newest first. A server SPEAKS by the same rule as a desktop (online, its doctor row `speech` ok or preparing). Its daemon reports that row like a desktop does: the CLI daemon runs the speech worker (`exponential __speech-worker`) only while one of the member's agents runs on it, headless (no microphone, no speakers): it probes once at start (no CUDA driver = no download, `speech` missing · No usable GPU at once), loads the voice when rung (inside the ring) and exits it after `serverIdleMs` without a call. It answers `call_ring` as a desktop does (`voice.callHostTicket({callId, deviceId})`, the same flow events, opening and replies on the call's stream). A server that cannot speak (no GPU, offline, failed, never reported) falls back exactly as a desktop does, the caller sees `Voice on {device}`; nothing else speaks = the SERVER's reason (`{server} can't speak: no usable GPU`), even with no desktop at all (`noDesktop` only when no candidate exists). No new UI: the server's `speech` row shows on its device page like a desktop's. Another member's server (a shared one) stays never rung. EXP-1857 (voice per agent, phase b of #EXP-1847, 2026-11-15; SUPERSEDES NEW-55's 'only the member's voice device' and NEW-99's `notHere` for the telephone): A CALL RINGS THE AGENT'S DEVICE. Where a call's speech runs = pure `callTarget(input)` (`targetCases`) ×4 and on the server (`voice.startCall`): input = `here` (THIS client's own desktop id; null on phones and web), `agentDevice` (the called agent's Runs on), `desktops` (the member's OWN desktops, newest `lastSeenAt` first, each `{id, name, online, speech, meeting}`: `speech` = its doctor row through `callSpeechOf`, `meeting` = a meeting runs on it) and `busy`. A desktop SPEAKS when it is online, holds no meeting and its speech is `ok` or `preparing` (a downloading voice rings until it is ready). The target is the first desktop that speaks of: the agent's device (only when it is one of the member's own desktops: a server before phase c, a phone, another member's machine never), then THE DESKTOP YOU'RE AT (`here`; Danny 2026-11-15: no voice-device setting, the fallback is automatic), then the member's other desktops in order. `fallback` = the target is not the agent's device; `local` = the target is `here` (the IDE runs the call itself, as before); else the client STREAMS to the target over the relay: phones, web AND NOW THE DESKTOP IDE (caller mode, the same wire). No desktop speaks: disabled with the reason of the first candidate (the agent's desktop, else here, else the newest desktop) read through `callAvailability` (offline, meeting, preparing, voiceFailed, noGpu); no desktop at all = `reasons.noDesktop`. A target found while `busy` = `reasons.busy`. Every member desktop prepares the voice (the worker and its `speech` doctor row), and push to talk and the wake word listen on the desktop you're at. The caller SEES WHICH DEVICE SPEAKS: `start {device, language, fallback}` keeps `fallback`, and `callView` gains `via` = `copy.via` with the device while the call falls back (null otherwise), drawn as a second status line under the status/timer in the status text style, truncated to one line, testId `testIds.via` (web, desktop panel, iOS, Android; the pill stays as it is; specimen `in call, falling back`). TRANSPORT: `voice.startCall` answers `{callId, ticket, url, relayUrl, deviceId, device, fallback}` (the target it picked; the caller ticket names it, the relay rings it); `voice.callHostTicket({callId, deviceId?})` mints the answer for the answering desktop (one of the member's own devices; an old IDE without `deviceId` = the voice device). A desktop that is rung answers whether or not it is the Assistant's device. iOS BACKGROUND (App Review 2.5.4 rejected 0.14.112, 2026-11-09; SUPERSEDES the BACKGROUND rule below for iOS): the iOS app declares no `audio` background mode, so an iOS call ENDS when the app leaves the foreground (screen locked, another app in front) like End call (a reason-less `call_end` to the host); Android keeps its `microphone` foreground service. EXP-1681 (phone call pill, 2026-11-03; approved in look parity round 2): THE PHONES MINIMIZE A CALL INTO THE DESKTOP'S FLOATING PILL. The phone's full-screen call surface gets a round icon button at its top leading corner (`icons.minimize`, label `copy.minimize` as tooltip and accessibility label, testId `testIds.minimize`, the ghost icon button, never words); it and the system back (Android) / a swipe down on the surface (iOS) MINIMIZE the call: the surface goes, the call goes on. While a call runs minimized THE PILL floats over every screen of the app (the app root's overlay, where the toasts live: above the tab bar, under a sheet): the same row as the desktop's (testId `pill`, the `call-pill` styleguide entry: the drag handle, the agent's avatar small, the name over the timer (ringing: the status), VoiceWave sm, then the round mute and the red end buttons at the compact size; speaker stays on the full screen), height `pill.height`, width `pill.width` but never wider than the screen minus 2 × `pill.marginPx`; the name and the status truncate. It is DRAGGABLE by any point outside its buttons and stays inside the safe area, `pill.marginPx` from every edge; its position is remembered on the device (default: horizontally centred, its bottom edge `pill.phoneBottomPx` above the safe area's bottom, clear of the floating tab bar). A TAP outside its buttons opens the full-screen surface again. A new call always opens full screen; the call's end removes both. The desktop keeps its rule (the pill while no IDE window is focused); web has no pill (its call is the full-height overlay) and draws the specimen only. NEW-99 (2026-10-30; SUPERSEDES the availability order below where they differ; EXP-1991 above supersedes its own): THE TELEPHONE NAMES WHAT IS MISSING AND WHERE TO FIX IT. The voice device is the member's Assistant's Runs on device (agent-settings.json `assistant`), so availability gains input `agent` (the member has a voice Assistant: `voice.get` agentId non-null) and the order is: no Assistant → `noAgent` (it points at Settings → Agents, where the Assistant is set up); an Assistant whose Runs on is not one of the member's desktops (no voice device) → `noVoiceDevice` (move it to a desktop on its own page, Settings → Assistant); offline → `offline`; meeting → `meeting`; a desktop that is not the voice device → `notHere`; no `speech` row → `preparing`; speech `failed` → `voiceFailed`; `noGpu` → `noGpu`; busy → `busy`. SPEECH ROW → CallSpeech is ONE pure mapper ×4, `callSpeechOf(doctor row state)` (`speechCases`: no row → null, ok → ok, missing → noGpu, error → failed, any other state (off = downloading, action) → preparing). The voice device's IDE reports `speech` error · `Download failed` (device-doctor.json) when the voice download failed before any voice was known or the worker crashed `MAX_CRASHES` times in a row, so a caller no longer reads a dead voice as getting ready forever; restarting Exponential there (or a changed setting) tries again. THE RUNS ON PICKER of an Assistant lists the member's desktops only (servers, CLI daemons and phones never speak, voice.json); a bound non-desktop stays listed so it still names itself. EXP-1423 (eTalk ring, 2026-10-29; SUPERSEDES the S-3 ring timing below; eTalk owns this call for Exponential and spezl): A CALL RINGS A RANDOM, REALISTIC FEW TIMES AND THE AGENT SPEAKS FIRST. The ring has no fixed length any more: the HOST draws one `random` in [0, 1) when the call starts (an injected number, so every mirror replays `ringCases` deterministically) and its earliest answer is `callRingMs(random)` = `constants.minRingMs` + floor(clamp(random, 0, 1) × `constants.ringJitterMs`); at that instant it steps `rang` (the same event as before). The ring ENDS when the voice device reports its warm-up done (`ready`, its worker's `CallListening` over the existing call wire), clamped: never before `callRingMs(random)`, and a `ready` that has not come by `constants.maxRingMs` fails the call `unavailable` (as before) = pure `callAnswerMs(random, readyMs)` (`answerCases`; readyMs null or ≥ `maxRingMs` = null, never answered; else the later of the two). Then it listens (#EXP-1966: no fixed greeting; the agent's own opening line, if any, is its first reply). WHY THESE NUMBERS: the cadence is the North American ringback every phone user knows from films and calls (ANSI T1.401: `constants.ringLowHz` + `constants.ringHighHz` together, `constants.ringToneMs` on, `constants.ringGapMs` off; Android plays exactly this as ToneGenerator TONE_CDMA_NETWORK_USA_RINGBACK); `minRingMs` 3000 keeps the old fixed ring as the floor (a warm device never answers sooner than today, always after one full ring, inside its first gap); `ringJitterMs` 6000 = one ring period, so the earliest pick-up spreads over a second ring (1 or 2 rings, never the same twice), and a cold device (a model still loading or downloading) simply keeps ringing in the same cadence until it is ready. The RING TONE ×4 is one cadence: `callRingToneOn(ms since the ring started)` (`ringToneCases`, true = the tone sounds) and it LOOPS until the call leaves `ringing` (answered, cancelled, failed; at most `maxRingMs`): web `playRingTone`, iOS `CallRingTone`, Android `VoiceCallAudio.ring`, the desktop worker's `ring_tone` on a local call's output stream (the host asks it to ring up to `maxRingMs`, its first Speak, the opening, or the pickup stops it). A remote call rings on the caller only (as before); the caller never draws a random: it follows the host's `rang` / `ready`. Phases, events, views and copy are unchanged (no dialing or connected phase: `start` is ringing, `rang` + `ready` answer it). S-3 (voice call ×4, 2026-10-28; SUPERSEDES the older text below where they differ; mockup = the S-3 plan card's `call` picture). A CALL RINGS FIRST: `start {device, language}` = phase `ringing` (view activity `ringing`, status `copy.calling`, only the round end button labelled `copy.cancel`); the ring lasts at least `callRingMs(random)` (a ring tone plays on the calling client, never on a remote voice device) and meanwhile the voice device WARMS UP: the worker is prepared, the speech recognizer and the voice are loaded (a download included), the microphone (a local call; a remote call takes the caller's stream) and the call's ONE output stream are opened. The worker confirms with its `CallListening` event = flow event `ready`; the ring's end = `rang`. Both (either order) = ANSWERED: phase listening (#EXP-1966: no fixed greeting any more; the agent's own opening line arrives as a reply, `replyStarted`, and speech over it barges in like any reply). `rang` without `ready` keeps ringing with status `copy.gettingReady`; ready without rang keeps `copy.calling`; partials and utterances during the ring are not the call's (dropped). A voice that is still not ready after `constants.maxRingMs`, or whose download fails, fails the call `unavailable`. A remote caller steps the host's `rang` / `ready` / `noSound` events like the others (`call_event`), so caller and host show the same ring; `call_ready` alone answers nothing (the old `connected` event and the `connecting` phase are gone). MIC CHECK: while ringing the host watches the microphone's `level` (talk-listen.json): when no frame reached `constants.noSoundLevel` by the ring's end it steps `noSound`, and while listening with an empty caption the caption reads `copy.noSound` until the first partial or utterance; the voice device logs the input device it opened (name + rate) at every call. SPEAK-BACK IS ALWAYS ON: availability no longer reads Speak replies (the setting is gone, voice.json), and `preparing` now only means the voice device has not reported its `speech` row yet: a voice that is downloading RINGS until it is ready. PHONE-CALL UI ×4 (WhatsApp / Teams style; `callView(state, platform)`): a full-screen surface (phones full screen, web a full-height overlay, the desktop's in-window CALL PANEL over the agent chat's body), top to bottom: the agent's avatar large and centred (its mark, the Assistant the Exponential logo) with a ring that pulses with `activity` (ringing: a soft halo pulse; listening: the success ring glowing with the level; speaking: the wave; thinking: dim; muted: none), the agent's name (title), the `status` line (null = the call's TIMER, `callTimer(ms since answered)`: `timerCases`, mm:ss, h:mm:ss from an hour, testId `timer`), the `caption` (centred, at most 4 lines, quoted utterances, the reply's sentence), and at the bottom the ROUND ICON-ONLY CALL BUTTONS in `buttons` order (styleguide entry `call-controls`; the APP-LEVEL `CallButton`, an Exponential call control rather than a low-level eUI primitive: web `CallButton` in `@exp/ui` call-controls.tsx, desktop `call_button` in exponential-ui-gpui controls/buttons.rs, iOS `CallButton` in ExpUI CallControls.swift, Android `CallButton` in ui/components/CallControls.kt): `mute` (icon `icons.mute`, toggled = `icons.unmute` on the inverted neutral fill; label `copy.mute` / `copy.unmute` as tooltip and accessibility label), `speaker` (PHONES only: the loudspeaker vs the earpiece, device-local, default on; `icons.speaker` / `icons.speakerOff`, labels `copy.speaker` / `copy.speakerOff`; event `speaker {on}`), and `end` (the RED round button, `icons.end`, `destructive` fill; while ringing labelled `copy.cancel` and the label shows UNDER it, otherwise `copy.endCall` as tooltip only). No text pills, no state word (`Listening` etc. stay accessibility values of the avatar). DESKTOP: the in-window panel replaces the old capsule while an IDE window of this device is focused and not minimized; the FLOATING PILL (testId `pill`, the `call-controls` entry's compact row: a drag handle, the avatar small, the name over the timer, the VoiceWave sm, the mute and end buttons) shows ONLY while no IDE window is focused (all minimized or another app in front): a transparent always-on-top window of FIXED size `pill.width` × `pill.height` (never resized or reopened while the text changes: the name and caption truncate), DRAGGABLE by any point outside its buttons (X11 override-redirect windows get no WM move: the pill tracks the pointer itself from press to release), its position remembered device-locally (default: bottom centre of the display under the pointer, `pill.marginPx` above its edge; a remembered position off every display falls back to it). Esc in the call panel or the pill and the tray's `End call` (voice.json `trayEndCall`) end the call. While THIS client runs the call the agent header's telephone is not disabled: it shows the panel. `busy` = a call this client does not run. Phones and web keep the screen awake while the surface shows (as before). NEW-55 (voice V4, phase-2 plan approved 2026-10-27 on #NEW-9): CALLER MODE. A call = a conversation with ONE agent by voice: the microphone stays open until End call, every finished utterance goes out as a plain message through `sessions.send` (the member's conversation with that agent, exactly like push to talk), every reply of that agent in that conversation is spoken, speech while a reply plays cancels it (barge-in), and an utterance finished while the agent's turn runs rides the existing queue bar (the `queue` slot strip) like a typed message. Recognition and the voice run ONLY on the member's voice device (`user_voice_settings.voiceDeviceId`); phones (V5) and web (V6) STREAM the call's audio to it. ENTRY: the telephone (icon concept `voice-call`, testId `testIds.call`, label `copy.call`) in the AGENT CHAT'S HEADER ×4, left of the overflow, the existing header icon button; never in the Agents list. The IDE tray's `Call {agent}` item (voice.json `trayCall`) calls the voice agent. AVAILABILITY = pure `callAvailability(input)` (`availabilityCases`; reasons in order, first match wins): no voice device → `noVoiceDevice`; Speak replies off → `speakOff` (the voice is only prepared while it is on); the voice device offline → `offline`; on a desktop that is NOT the voice device → `notHere` (V4 calls only from the voice device's own IDE); the voice device's doctor row `speech` (group voice) missing or not yet checked → `preparing`; its state `missing` (no usable GPU: Qwen3-TTS runs on the GPU only) → `noGpu`; a call already running on the voice device → `busy`; else enabled (reason null). A disabled telephone stays visible, dimmed, its tooltip = the reason (web, desktop: a disabled control takes no press); #EXP-1878 on a PHONE (no hover) a TAP shows it: THE info toast with the reason, the telephone keeps its press while dimmed and never calls (`callTap(platform, availability)`, `tapCases`; no long-press tooltip). FLOW = pure `callStep(state, event)` + `callView(state)` (`flowCases`; the SAME machine on the voice device and on a caller, which receives the host's events as `call_event` frames): phases connecting → listening ⇄ thinking ⇄ speaking, `muted` is a flag (the microphone closes, replies still play); `view` null = no call surface. The call surface: on the desktop THE voice capsule (voice-call-overlay: VoiceWave md, `state` bold, `line` muted, then the `mute` pill and the PRIMARY `copy.endCall` pill), on phones full screen and on web a centred card (the `voice-call` entry: VoiceWave xl, the state, the line, End call primary + Mute); a failure ends the call with a toast (`toast`): `copy.failed` by code, the relay's `busy` included; a web browser without WebCodecs Opus keeps the telephone enabled (availability never asks) and a press toasts `unsupported` without dialing (#NEW-70: Opus only, no PCM wire kind). `surfaceSpecimens` are the styleguide rows of both surfaces (web + desktop `voice-call-overlay` capsules with the lead pill, and the `voice-call` entry); each view's End call pill is `copy.endCall`. TRANSPORT (streamed calls): tRPC `voice.startCall({agentId})` answers `{callId, ticket, url, relayUrl}` (the client dials `url` as-is) or refuses with the availability reason; the caller opens the steer relay with a `caller` ticket (claims callId, deviceId, deviceOwnerId); the relay rings the voice device on its control socket (`{t:'call_ring', callId, agentId}`), which mints a `call_host` ticket (tRPC `voice.callHostTicket({callId})`) and joins; both get `{t:'call_ready'}`; no host within `constants.ringTimeoutMs` → the caller gets `{t:'error', code:'no_answer'}` then `bye`. The `call_host` ticket names the voice device (`deviceId`) and is admitted only into that device's room. Once paired, each socket may send at most `constants.maxFramesPerSecond` binary frames per second (a token bucket; extra frames are dropped), a call ends after `constants.maxCallMs` (reason `max_length`) and after `constants.idleTimeoutMs` without a frame either way (reason `idle`): both sides get `call_end` with that reason. A `call_end` reaches the flow as `hungUp {reason?}` (`hangUpRules`): a reason (`idle`, `max_length`, or `dropped` when the other socket went away) fails the call as `dropped` with its toast; ONLY a reason-less hang-up (the other side pressed End call) ends silently. Mute never stops the frames: a muted caller keeps sending silence (web its disabled track's, the phones ENCODED SILENCE, one `up` frame per `constants.frameMs`), so muting never trips `idle`. BACKGROUND: a phone call KEEPS RUNNING with the screen locked or another app in front (iOS the `audio` background mode with AVAudioSession playAndRecord / voiceChat, Android the `microphone` foreground service with its ongoing `Call {agent}` notification); only End call or the far side ends it, and while the call surface shows the screen never dims on its own. Another call taking the audio (an incoming phone call: iOS an AVAudioSession interruption that began now, never a late one carrying `wasSuspended`, Android audio focus LOSS or LOSS_TRANSIENT, or focus refused at start) fails the call as `dropped`; a route change mid-call (AirPods or another headset connecting or leaving) keeps the call: the phone rebuilds its capture for the new route's input format (#NEW-89); the call's end gives the routing back (iOS the session category from before the call, Android the mode and device once its audio threads have exited); signing out or switching accounts ends it. DEPLOY ORDER: the steer relay ships BEFORE web (an older relay refuses caller tickets with 401, which also count toward its failed-auth rate limit). The voice device answers every ring without asking: a caller is always the device's own member. AUDIO = BINARY WebSocket frames: byte 0 = kind (`wire.kinds`), bytes 1-2 = sequence (u16 big-endian, wraps), then ONE Opus packet of `constants.frameMs` ms; uplink mono `constants.upRate` Hz at ~`constants.upKbps` kbps (web and the voice device's encoder add in-band FEC; the phones' platform encoders expose no FEC switch and send none), downlink mono `constants.downRate` Hz at ~`constants.downKbps` kbps; a frame above `wire.maxFrameBytes` is dropped; a caller may send only `up`, the host only `down`. CONTROL = JSON text frames `wire.control`; the relay forwards them between the pair, persists nothing and never decodes audio. It CAN read both, the events' words and the Opus, until the call seal is on (EXP-1941 above). The caller plays the downlink through a `constants.jitterMs` ms jitter buffer, flushed on `call_event` speechStarted (barge-in), and captures with the OS echo canceller on (iOS `.voiceChat`, Android VOICE_COMMUNICATION + AcousticEchoCanceler, web `echoCancellation: true`); the voice device's own microphone runs through the worker's echo canceller with the reply as the reference (#NEW-92, desktop only: ONE output stream per local call, and barge-in and turns pass talk-listen.json `echoGate`: the canceller's output only, a stricter gate until it converged, an utterance made of the reply's own words dropped). In a call the worker closes a segment after `constants.minSilenceMs` ms of silence (push to talk keeps talk-listen.json's 300) and barge-in needs `constants.bargeInMs` ms of speech. MICROPHONE OWNERSHIP (#1265 review, talk-listen.json `micOwnerCases`): a call takes precedence on the voice device: it closes the wake word's microphone (a wake turn in flight ends unanswered), the wake scan pauses for the whole call (a remote call keeps the device's microphone closed), and the scan comes back after Hangup; a push-to-talk Listen during a call is refused (`empty`, the call goes on; the IDE never sends one: the key waits for End call). #NEW-57: while a meeting runs on the voice device (voice settings `meetingStartedAt` set) the telephone is disabled with `reasons.meeting` (checked after `offline`, before `notHere`), and a call request that reaches the device anyway fails with `failed.meeting`. #EXP-1936: a ring that reaches a desktop already in a call the relay does not know (a LOCAL call: the relay's `busy` covers streamed calls only) is refused the same way with `failed.busy`: the desktop joins as the host, sends `call_event` failed `busy` once `call_ready` came and hangs up; the call it runs goes on. Nothing new on the wire (a host on an older build does not answer such a ring and the caller reads `no_answer`). #EXP-1936: a caller steps ONLY the `call_event`s listed under `wire.control` (a host's `start`, `mute`, `unmute` or `speaker` is ignored; its `end` or `hungUp` ends the call as a `call_end` would), and a settings change that takes the worker away mid-call (the Assistant removed) ends the call as `failed.dropped`, like a worker that died. A HOST that fails the call (its voice never got ready, its worker died, its microphone failed) sends `call_event {event: {t: 'failed', code}}` BEFORE its `call_end`, so the caller fails with the same `copy.failed` toast instead of the reason-less hang-up's silent end; a caller steps a host `failed` with any code it has copy for, anything else as `dropped`.

callSession.$comment: EXP-1961 (2026-11-18, phases 2 and 3 of #EXP-1943, decided by Danny): A CALL RUNS IN ITS OWN CALL SESSION, A CHILD OF THE CHAT. WHICH CHAT: the caller's conversation with the called agent (the one `sessions.send {agentId}` reaches; created if missing). START: the HOST asks for it while it rings: `voice.callSession({agentId, callId})` (tRPC only, never MCP; the member's own call: the agent must be one they may call, `memberAgent`), so a desktop that runs the call locally (it never calls `voice.startCall`) and a caller of any age get the same call session; the host asks once per call (a reconnect asks again with the same callId). #EXP-1981: a STREAMED call names the ring's call id; a call a desktop runs itself sends NO callId (never an empty one: the input takes it absent or non-empty). A SEALED call (#EXP-1941) asks once its key source has adopted the chat's root (a first call's chat is created there): the daemon as soon as that root is known, before the caller's first frame opened; the IDE when the call begins, after it. Its `ready` waits for that answer as it waits for the opening line (a pickup at `openingWaitMs` without it counts as silent), nothing is spoken from the chat meanwhile, what is said meanwhile is held and sent once it answered (into the call session, or the chat on null; into the chat when the call ends first), a session that answers after the hang-up is told the hang-up (`voice.callEnded`), and null takes the old path at once; the opening line, the utterances and the reply watch then follow the call session exactly as in a clear call. It picks with pure `callSessionPick(prev, nowMs)` (`pickCases`) over the chat's newest call child `prev` ({status, endedAtMs} of its `sessions.voice_call`; null = none): no call child, or an ENDED one = `start`; a live one whose call is running (`endedAtMs` null: a reconnect) or ended at most `resumeMs` ago = `resume`; one ended longer ago = `replace` (that one ends now, quietly: no second report, then `start`). `start` = `sessions.send {parentId: chat, name: title.en}` (a server line, legal in a keyed tree) with the `request` text ({language} = the agent's Voice language name, `languageNames`, English when unset) as its first message, the child marked as a call (`sessions.voice_call` = {callId, startedAt, segmentStartedAt, endedAt: null, durationMs: 0, summaryPending: false, readUpTo: now}; the mark is the server's, like `meeting: true`: never on the wire). It runs on the chat's device with the chat's runner (a child's usual inheritance), sealed with the tree's key like everything in the tree (#EXP-1941). Its brief (session-brief.json `callCases`): the Request, then a Call section instead of Parent (the chat's title and id, the recent plaintext messages, the open work); its launch adds the voice section (coding `skill.rs`, `brief.call`). `resume` = the same row: `segmentStartedAt` = now, `endedAt` null, `summaryPending` false, and the `resumeText` as its next message (an idle session wakes; a turn still running takes it at its next edge). Both answer {sessionId, chatId, resumed}; a chat whose call session cannot start (the tree is full, the device refused) answers null and the host falls back to the old path (utterances into the chat). OPENING (#FEED-275, no fixed greeting any more): the call session's FIRST reply after the `request` (or the `resumeText`) is the agent's own opening line, written and synthesized during the ring. Pure `callOpening(readyAtMs, openingAtMs, nowMs)` (`openingCases`, the Rust hosts replay it): ready = the host's `ready` (the voice is in, `hostVoice`); before ready = `wait`; an opening already in at ready, or arriving within `openingWaitMs` after it = `speak` (said in the agent's voice, shown as its line); none by `readyAtMs + openingWaitMs` = `listen`: the host picks up silently on Listening and that call's opening is never spoken (it stays in the transcript). NO FIXED GREETING (#EXP-1966): `copy.greeting` is gone and `answered` goes straight to listening on all four platforms; a call without its own session (an older server, no chat yet) picks up silently too. The host still steps `replyFinished` at the pickup, so an older caller whose machine still shows the greeting at `answered` leaves it at once and shows Listening. A late opening after a silent pickup is dropped only while nothing was said yet (a later reply answers the caller). DURING THE CALL: each utterance is a person message into the CALL SESSION (sealed with the tree's key as before, #EXP-1930); the host reads aloud the call session's replies, never the chat's. #EXP-2015: the Speaking banner of a call session's reply (voice.json: Dock `Banner`, Stop) shows in the CHAT's Dock, where the call runs (the call session's own view has no Dock). Before an utterance lands, the server copies the CHAT's messages newer than `readUpTo` (a person's, and the chat agent's own plain replies; no cards, nothing the call session wrote) into the call session as pending input authored by the chat (`Message from <chat> (session <id>): …`, a sealed body as a byte copy: same tree, same key), in order, then the utterance, and moves `readUpTo`: the call reads what was typed in the chat before its next answer, and typing in the chat never wakes the call. #EXP-2014: the call session's own server lines (the `resumeText`, the `endedText`) carry no copy: the chat's catch-up waits for the next utterance, so the reply to the `resumeText` answers it alone and is the opening line, never a reply to a chat message. The call does small things itself (look-ups, filing an issue); bigger work it sends to the chat (`exponential_sessions_send` to its parent). Its turn replies never reach the chat (eagent bus.json: a call child's turn is skipped for its parent). HANG-UP: the host calls `voice.callEnded({sessionId, callId})` once per hang-up (either side, a drop too): `endedAt` = now, `durationMs` += now - `segmentStartedAt` (`durationCases`, pure `callDuration`), `summaryPending` = true, and the `endedText` ({minutes} = `callTimer` of this segment) as the call session's next message. Its next reply is the call's summary: delivered to the chat as a WAKING `report` card {kind: report, sessionId, summary, final: false, call: {startedAt, endedAt, durationMs}} (bus.json; a sealed summary rides as the body, its card summary empty), `summaryPending` cleared. The session then idles for the resume window; the next call past it ends it (`replace`). FOR THE UI (phase 4, not here): a call session is `sessions.voice_call` non-null (synced in the sessions shape): running = `endedAt` null; the card in the chat is the child's `session` card (posted at start) plus each `report` card with `call`; duration = `durationMs` (+ the running segment).
callSession.request: The person is calling you and the phone is ringing. Answer with ONE short opening line in your own words that fits where the chat stands, in {language}, then wait for them to speak.
callSession.resumeText: The person called back. Open again with ONE short line in {language}, then wait.
callSession.endedText: The call ended after {minutes}. Reply with the call's summary for the main chat, nothing else: what was said and decided, what you did, and what you handed to the chat. Plain sentences, no greeting.

caller.$comment: EXP-1993 (2026-11-19, decided by Danny; the spec of `caller.cases`): THE PHONE'S CALLER IS ONE PURE MACHINE. `callerStep(state, input)` answers the next state and the effects in order (iOS: ExpCore `VoiceCall.Caller`, Android: `VoiceCall.Caller`, web: @exp/etalk `callerStep`, #EXP-2017; each replays every case); `VoiceCallClient` (iOS) and `VoiceCallController` (Android) only do the effects and hand in what happened. STATE: the flow (`callStep`, `flowCases`), `stage` (`idle`; `holding` = the tap went, the hold is asked; `asking` = it rings, the ticket is asked; `dialed` = the ticket's url was dialled; `paired` = `call_ready` came) and `sealed` (the ticket's `seal`). A case feeds `events` from the idle state and expects, per event, the `effects` in order, then the final `stage` and `phase` (and `device`, `fallback`, `muted`, `speaker` where given). INPUTS (`t`): `start {device, language, fallback}` = the tap (idle only; `callTarget` named the device); `held {ok, code?}` = the hold's answer (a refusal fails the call with `code`, none = `dropped`); `ticket {device?, fallback?, sealed?}` = `voice.startCall`'s usable answer (EXP-1857: its device and fallback replace the tap's; none = the tap's stay; told sealed without the claim or the ids is no usable answer but `failed dropped`); `refused {message}` = its refusal in the platform's own words; `frame {frame}` = one control frame off the socket (a sealed call's opened by its line first, `seal`); `closed` = the socket went away; `failed {code, told?}` = the call's own failure (the audio, Android's service refused later, a dead path by `callPathDead`, iOS's microphone refused during `ticket`; `told` = a seal failure whose line already sent its own `call_end {reason}`); `ringTimeout` = the ring's bound passed; `mute`, `speaker` = the buttons (toggles); `end` = End call (also an account switch and, iOS BACKGROUND, the app leaving the foreground). EFFECTS (`do`): `hold` (Android: the audio focus and the microphone service, EXP-1942, its grant asked before the tap; iOS holds nothing and answers `held ok` at once), `ring {ms}` (the ring tone, looped; `ringTimeout` after `ms` = `constants.maxRingMs`), `ticket` (iOS asks for the microphone first, then both wait for a key holder and call `voice.startCall`), `dial`, `startAudio` (the microphone and the playback), `stopRing` (answered: the call's timer starts), `flush` (barge-in: the buffered reply goes), `mute {muted}`, `speaker {on}`, `send {frame}` (on the call's socket; nothing while it still connects, and a socket that connects after the end is closed, EXP-1940), `alive` (`call_alive`: the liveness deadline starts, `livenessCases`), `release` (everything the call holds: the ring, the audio, the socket, the service, the seal line, the timers) and `toast {text}`. RULES: a call ends once; after its end every input of that call is ignored (a new `start` begins the next one), so every frame after a host's `failed` is ignored, whatever each platform does with its socket. End call sends `call_end` before `release` once dialled. AN OWN FAILURE sends `call_end {reason: dropped}` before `release` once dialled (the host learns it from the caller, not from the relay's guess), except when `told`; before the dial there is nobody to tell. An end from the far side sends nothing: `call_end {reason?}` steps `hungUp` (`hangUpRules`), `error {code}` and `bye {outcome}` fail with `Seal.wireCode` of it (none = `dropped`), `closed` fails `dropped`. A host's `call_event` steps only `wire.control`'s events: `failed {code}` fails with `Seal.wireCode(code)` (a code without copy reads `dropped`), `speechStarted` flushes first, its `end` / `hungUp` end the call as a `call_end` would (#EXP-1936), its `start`, `mute`, `unmute` and `speaker` are ignored. `call_mute` goes only once paired and never on a sealed call. The ring's bound fails `unavailable` while the call still rings, as an own failure. WEB (#EXP-2017): `apps/web/src/lib/voice-call/call.ts` executes `callerStep` (packages/etalk `voice-call.ts`); a browser holds nothing (its `hold` answers `held ok` at once, iOS's way: the microphone is asked with the `ticket`) and has no earpiece (`speaker` switches nothing). The desktop IDE's dialled call (`etalk-gpui` `voice_call.rs`) replays none of these cases but follows them: a host's `end` / `hungUp`, the ring's bound, and its own failure's `call_end {reason: dropped}` (a path gone silent is told by its socket, `steer` `call_caller.rs`); after a host's `failed` it still hangs up with a reason-less `call_end`.
